text.p: Miami Computer Supply Corp Chairman Anthony Liberati said Friday he expect the company's full-year earnings per share to total about $0.52, exceeding analysts' estimates by $0.02 per share.

In a phone interview with Reuters, Liberati said his estimate is based on expectations that the company will continue its first quarter performance of $0.13 per share for the remaining three quarters of the year.
According to First Call the company is expected to earn $0.50 per share for the year.
Liberati said his estimate does not include potential acquisitions.
He said the company will remain true to its policy of acquiring only companies that will be immediately accretive to earnings.

Over the past five years Miami Computer has bought six computer and office automation companies, including the deal it struck earlier this week to acquire the computer supply and office automation business of Imperial Data Supply Corp for undisclosed terms.

Miami Computer said the acquisition provides it with a significant entry into the Northwest market. Imperial has its headquarters in Spokane, Wash., and offices in Idaho Falls, Idaho, and Missoula, Montana.
"Our annualized run rate at Miami Computer is $80 million in revenues," said chief financial officer Michael Peppel. "Within a year, the acquisition will add another $10 million in yearly revenues."
Peppel and Liberati said they want to expand throughout the country and overseas through acquisitions.
"We're in discussions with a multitude of people," Peppel said.
Miami Computer Supply went public late last year at $8.50 a share. The stock closed today at 9-1/2, up 1/4.

Miami Computer distributes computer and office automation supplies and accessories, including a line of computer projection presentation products. The company's products include consumable supplies, such as laser toner, copier toner, media products and fax supplies.
Peppel said it's a growing market and it is expected that in 1998, for the first time, revenues from computer printer supplies will exceed revenues from selling the printers themselves.
Miami Computer is the only publicly traded end-user computer supply company.
"The market has never differentiated between office supply and computer supply," Liberati said. "But they really are two different types of business."
